world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Hooley, Bruce A. 1976. Austronesian languages: Morobe Province. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 2, Pacific Linguistics C-39, 335-348.
sources.note: Classification and lexicostatistic percentages only; Wampur named four times ('In the Wanton Valley'; Markham Sub-Family member); no occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent'.

Cites Holzknecht 1989 for subclassification only; the WORLD_TARGETS record shows n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0 and three overview-type references (Holzknecht 1989, Hooley 1971, Smith 1988), all examined above.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog: resources in and about the Wampur language (waz), as of 2025-11-04 (via Wayback)
sources.note: Lists nine 1985 audio items by Susanne Holzknecht (PARADISEC SH2-ANUA520_3501 to 3509), plus Glottolog and Ethnologue entries; no written language description of any kind is listed.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: ANU. viii+228 pp. (hdl 1885/145647)
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.3 Wampur, p. 52 (PDF p. 60): phoneme table 4.4 (consonants p b c j k g ʔ, mp nt nc ŋk ŋʔ, m n ŋ, s h, r, w y; vowels i a u) with five notes on allophony (/b/ [b~β] finally, /k, ŋk/ rare and borrowed from Adzera, /r/ ~ [d] ~ [l], only like-vowel sequences which may be broken by a glottal stop). Nothing on stress. Ch. 4 intro, p. 50: 'In this chapter I first give a brief phonological statement of each of the Markham languages. Full phonological statements are to be published at a later date, with grammar sketches of these languages.' The word 'stress' occurs 4 times in the whole book,…

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne C. 1988. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea: a history of the Austronesian languages of the Markham Valley. PhD thesis, ANU (hdl 1885/133945)
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.3 Wampur: identical phoneme table and notes to the 1989 book; no statement on stress ('stress' hits in the thesis are the same four passages as the book: Adzera/Sukurum vowel note, Watut final -ʔ, a dialect-perception remark, a bibliographic title).

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of Western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: Wampur appears 31 times, only as reflexes inside cognate sets (e.g. Wampur mon ti, hio-, zah, hani, ri-nciʔ, cim); the passages on stress (pp. around lines 3991-4003, Verner-type lenition) concern Ali and Kairiru, not Markham languages. Nothing on Wampur stress.

sources.citation: Smith, Geoffrey P. 1988. Morobe counting systems. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 1-132. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/253560)
sources.note: Sec. 27 Wampur, pp. 68-69: numerals 1-20 recorded by S. Holzknecht in Wampur village (bisangcwa, iriciru, iruc a bits...), transcribed without stress marks; the transcription conventions (p. 54) only introduce a symbol for an 'unaccented neutral vowel'. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne (collector). Markham languages fieldwork, 1985-88. ANU Open Research hdl 1885/123380, doi 10.4225/72/5911e78b2c85e (PARADISEC SH2)
sources.note: Audio recordings of informant interviews for the 15 Markham languages; no written description; PARADISEC catalogue page itself returned 403.

sources.citation: Hooley, Bruce A. & K. A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Morobe District, New Guinea. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, PL C-13, 1065-1094.
sources.note: One mention of Wampur (village whose language is a Family member, 50% cognate figure); no phonology, no stress.

sources.note: Adzera is Wampur's closest relative (all Wampur speakers also speak Adzera, Holzknecht 1989: 28); a stress statement for Adzera would be the nearest comparative proxy but is NOT a Wampur statement.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. Fuller phonological statement and grammar sketch of Wampur, announced in Holzknecht 1989: 50 ('Full phonological statements are to be published at a later date, with grammar sketches of these languages')

sources.note: The only fieldworker on Wampur promised a full phonology; if any manuscript or field notes exist (ANU/PARADISEC SH2 collection), it would be the first place a Wampur stress rule could be stated. No trace of a publication found in Glottolog, OLAC or hh.bib.
